title: Jim Kelly and Ernest Kelly, and going to Mexico
summary: He identifies Jim Kelly as the chambon player in his carnival band, notes Kelly's death from diabetes, and says they went to Mexico together.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Ask him what Jim Harris played in it.
He said, what did Jim Harris play? Jim Harris?
In that first band, your name?
In that first band, your name?
With a carnival. With a carnival.

Jim Kelly, yeah. Chambon. That was Ernest Kelly's anchor. We didn't know Ernest Kelly. Didn't have his name either. Yeah, I have his name. He's a trauma. Chambon, yeah. Dead fish brother. He had diabetes. He took me cutting his legs off. Took me apart.
Died. Ask him, did he ever work again with Jim Kelly.
Sometime but he went with him.
For sure. He said, did you ever work again with Jim Kelly?
Again? Yeah, with him. Yeah. You mean with Jim Kelly? We went to Mexico together. But I'll tell you the way. But I should work with his next one, Ernest, with Bob Lyon. He got his name, Mr. Bob Lyon.
